summary: The note explains how local businesses are using social media marketing to attract customers, with adoption surging since September 2023. It covers social commerce, influencer partnerships, user-generated content, algorithm changes, video content and paid advertising, citing statistics from consultants and research firms. It concludes that social media marketing is now a critical component of local business strategy and is reshaping local economies.
one_line: Local businesses increasingly rely on social commerce, influencers, user content, video and paid ads, making social media marketing essential to local economies.
key_facts: Since September 2023, there has been a marked surge in local businesses adopting social media marketing strategies.
Instagram launched its enhanced shopping feature in late 2023, as detailed by Minneapolis-based retail consultant Ellen Marks on October 12th.
Ellen Marks said, "We've seen a 30% increase in sales among local retailers using Instagram Shopping."
Tyler Johnson of the marketing firm DataViz wrote in a November 2nd publication that influencer partnerships bring an average 22% uptick in foot traffic and an 18% rise in online interactions.
The Cozy Corner Bookstore in Portland ran a campaign asking readers to post selfies with their purchases; the hashtag #ReadLocalPortland reached over 50,000 mentions by January 2024.
Facebook's algorithm shift on February 3rd, 2024 prioritized personal over business content, forcing local businesses to refine their content strategies.
Local businesses embraced short-form video on TikTok and Instagram Reels from September 2023 through early 2024, e.g. Sarah Nguyen of "Sarah's Artisanal Chocolates".
A MarketPro report on March 20th, 2024 found local businesses increased social media advertising budgets by 25% year-over-year.
Paid social advertising allows precision targeting by demographics, interests and behaviors, and is a cost-effective alternative as traditional advertising costs soar.
Social commerce lets small businesses without sophisticated online storefronts compete with e-commerce giants by selling directly through social apps.
User-generated content acts as an informal endorsement, builds community around a brand and fosters loyalty and repeat business.
The note argues social media marketing is no longer optional but a critical component of a successful local business strategy in 2024 and beyond.
